title: Tesseract demo — voice-over storyboard
source: final model §7.1 (team design notes, 28 Oct 2026) with the 28 Oct fact fixes; numbers from src/data/summary.json, impact.json, meta.json
note: Synthetic, illustrative data. The real company is never named. SAP Business One is described as document-centric, never as unable to approve master data.

beats.vo: Amy needed one new item code. It took eighteen days, a bounced request and three approvers one at a time, and her sales order still failed.
beats.screen: /pitch/hook: black screen, "18 days.", day counter 1 → 18 over a faded email collage; caption "Scenario from case brief, App C".

It took 18 days, a bounced request and three approvers one at a time, and her sales order still failed.

beats.vo: At Lives Group, master data is created by email. Records arrive incomplete or duplicated, so the regional numbers can't be trusted. Tesseract fixes both ends.
beats.screen: Home: split "Clean in │ Money out"; badge "Runs on Microsoft 365 · lands in SAP Business One".
beats.title: Frame
beats.read: At Lives Group, / master data is created **by email**. // Records arrive **incomplete** or **duplicated**, / so the regional numbers **can't be trusted**. // Tesseract fixes **both ends**.

beats.vo: Amy's item is a blood collection tube: a lab consumable regulated as an IVD, an in-vitro diagnostic device. She pastes her old email, and the form fills itself. As an IVD, it needs a licence number, and Quality joins the route automatically: the step she missed last time. Before submitting, she sees her approvers, all in parallel, and her go-live date: Tuesday, the third of November.
beats.screen: Scene amy-intake: paste old email → fields fill ("K2EDTA Blood Collection Tube 4 mL, 100/pk", badge "cached for demo") → category "IVD medical device" → licence field turns red/required, QA/RA chip slides into the route → footer "QA/RA · BU Head · Business Support in parallel → MDM · Expected live Tue 3 Nov"; side note "3 waiting customer orders · S$36,000".

She pastes her old email, and the form fills itself.

beats.vo: Marcus is from a new business unit, Meridian Life Sciences. He types a hospital in shorthand, and Tesseract finds it already on file. So he extends that record to his entity, instead of creating a duplicate. Business Support and Finance check it, then MDM.
beats.screen: 4 s admin-marcus insert ("MLS — Meridian Life Sciences + approvers · Saved"), then marcus-dup: types "Natl Univ Hosp" → amber card "National University Hospital · C-SG-00017 · same tax ID" → clicks "Extend to my entity" → route "Business Support + Finance (Wei Jie) → MDM".

beats.vo: Wei Jie in Finance approves on a Teams card, where he already works. Credit terms never travel in the message. Only Finance and MDM can open them, inside Tesseract. Reminders go out before anything stalls, and every decision is logged.
beats.screen: weijie-teams: Teams card with "Credit terms: •••• · view in Tesseract (Finance only)" → open details (values visible to Wei Jie) → 2 s persona flip to Amy (••••) → Approve → tracker step turns green; chip "Reminder after 1 business day".

beats.vo: SAP Business One's built-in approvals are document-centric, designed around documents like sales orders. So approvals for master data live in Microsoft 365, and SAP stays the system of record. Priya clicks Generate SAP B1 import, and gets a Data Transfer Workbench file: the import format SAP already reads, with SAP's own field names. Sending it automatically, through SAP's Service Layer, is phase two. Today, she loads the file and marks the item created.
beats.screen: 4 s /architecture swimlane (path highlighted) → priya-sap: "Generate SAP B1 import" → DTW preview with SAP field names and the two header rows highlighted → Service Layer tab "Phase 2 · not sent" → "Mark created in SAP B1".

beats.read: SAP Business One's **built-in approvals** are **document-centric**, / designed around **documents** like sales orders. // So approvals for master data live in **Microsoft 365**, / and SAP stays the **system of record**. // Priya clicks **Generate SAP B1 import**, / and gets a **Data Transfer Workbench** file: / the import format SAP **already reads**, / with SAP's **own field names**. // Sending it **automatically**, / through SAP's Service Layer, / is **phase two**. // Today, / she loads the file / and marks the item **created**.

beats.vo: Amy is told the moment it's live. And stuck demand drops by thirty-six thousand dollars: three customer orders that were waiting on that one record.
beats.screen: Toast "Amy: your item is live" → cut to the Pulse stuck-demand tile counting down S$345,800 → S$309,800; toast "S$36,000 of customer orders unblocked".

beats.vo: Now, money out, on synthetic data. Regional Pulse compares the twelve months to September 2026 with the year before, on de-duplicated customers. Orders are fifty-three point four million dollars, up four percent. Merge the duplicates, and Bukit Damai, Malaysia's number-two account, is really down thirty-two percent. Each country card names an owner, an action and the dollars at stake. On this illustrative data, today's forecasting method is off by eleven units per hundred ordered; ours, by nine.

"Synthetic, illustrative" badge visible throughout.
